results.title: NiMet Forecasts Three Days of Rain, Thunderstorms Across Nigeria
results.description: Agency warns of flash floods, strong winds; advises motorists, residents, airlines to take precautions The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has forecast a mix of sunshine, cloudy conditions, thunderstorms and moderate rainfall across different parts of the country from Monday to Wednesday, with coastal communities in the South facing possible flash floods from persistent rains. In its weather outlook released in Abuja on Sunday, the agency said parts of the North would experience sunny skies with patches of clouds on Monday, while thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rainfall were expected in several states during the morning and later in the afternoon or evening. NiMet said Taraba, Adamawa and Kaduna could experience thunderstorms and moderate rains during the morning hours. It added that similar conditions were expected later in the day across parts of Borno, Bauchi, Gombe, Jigawa, Katsina, Kano, Kaduna, Adamawa and Taraba states. The forecast also indicated unsettled weather in the North Central region, with thunderstorms and moderate rainfall expected over parts of Plateau, Niger, Nasarawa and the Federal Capital Territory during the morning. According to the agency, the situation could intensify later in the day, with thunderstorms and moderate rains forecast across parts of Kogi, Benue, Plateau, Niger, Nasarawa and the FCT. Southern states to experience widespread rainfall The South is expected to record more widespread rainfall during the three-day period. NiMet forecast moderate rains over parts of Ondo, Ogun, Cross River, Akwa Ibom, Rivers, Lagos and Bayelsa states on Monday morning. By the afternoon and evening, moderate rainfall is expected across the entire southern region. The agency said similar conditions would persist on Tuesday, although the morning forecast would be relatively lighter in some areas. Parts of Cross River, Delta, Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom, Lagos and Rivers states are expected to experience light rainfall during the morning, while thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rains are forecast across the entire southern region later in the day. The agency's forecast for Wednesday also points to continued rainfall across the South. A cloudy atmosphere is expected to dominate the region in the morning, with light rains likely over parts of Edo, Cross River, Delta, Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom and Rivers states. NiMet said thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rainfall were expected across the entire southern region later in the day. More storms expected in the North For Tuesday, NiMet forecast thunderstorms and moderate rains over parts of Zamfara, Sokoto, Kebbi, Adamawa and Taraba states during the morning hours. The agency said the weather could become more unsettled later in the day, with thunderstorms and moderate rainfall expected over parts of Borno, Jigawa, Yobe, Bauchi, Gombe, Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Taraba and Adamawa states. In the North Central region, thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rains are expected over parts of Niger and Kwara states and the Federal Capital Territory in the morning. “Later during the afternoon or evening hours, thunderstorms with moderate rains are anticipated across the region,” the agency stated. On Wednesday, NiMet predicted partly cloudy skies over the northern region, with chances of thunderstorms accompanied by light rains over parts of Bauchi, Jigawa and Yobe states during the morning. It forecast thunderstorms with moderate rainfall across the region during the afternoon and evening. For the North Central, sunny skies with patches of clouds are expected in the morning before thunderstorms and moderate rains spread across the entire region later in the day. NiMet warns of flash floods Beyond the weather forecast, NiMet urged Nigerians to take precautions in areas where thunderstorms and heavy rainfall are expected. The agency warned that strong winds could precede thunderstorms and advised residents to secure loose objects that could be blown away and cause injuries or damage. It also issued a specific warning to communities in coastal areas of the South, where continuous rainfall could increase the risk of flash flooding. “Drivers should avoid driving or wading through floodwaters. Avoid driving in heavy rain. “Disconnect electrical appliances from electrical sockets. Stay away from tall trees to avoid impact from falling branches and broken trees,” it advised. The warnings come amid the recurring risk of flooding during periods of intense rainfall, particularly in low-lying and poorly drained communities. Residents are therefore advised to monitor local weather conditions and avoid unnecessary exposure during thunderstorms. Airlines advised to obtain airport-specific forecasts NiMet also called on airline operators to obtain airport-specific weather reports from the agency to support effective planning and safer flight operations. The agency encouraged members of the public to remain informed through its regular weather updates and consult its official website for additional information. With thunderstorms and rainfall expected in several parts of the country over the next three days, NiMet's forecast highlights the need for residents, motorists, businesses and transport operators to remain alert, particularly during periods of heavy rain and strong winds.
